title: Frank Ocean
wiki_lead:
Frank Ocean (born Christopher Edwin Breaux, October 28, 1987) is an American singer and songwriter. His accolades include two Grammy Awards and a Brit Award. He has been credited by several music critics as a pioneer of the alternative R&B genre.
Ocean began his musical career as a ghostwriter before joining the Los Angeles-based hip hop collective Odd Future in 2010. The year prior, he signed with RedZone Entertainment, an imprint of Def Jam Recordings, although his debut mixtape, Nostalgia, Ultra (2011), was released independently. His debut studio album, Channel Orange (2012) won Best Urban Contemporary Album; its lead single, "Thinkin Bout You", was nominated for Record of the Year. He was named by Time as one of the world's 100 most influential people in 2013.
After a four-year hiatus, Ocean released the visual album Endless (2016) to fulfill contractual obligations with Def Jam. His second studio album, Blonde, was released independently the following day. Blonde was met with critical praise, and debuted atop the US Billboard 200. After 2017, Ocean has released sporadic singles, worked as a photographer for magazines, launched the fashion brand Homer, and started Homer Radio. Ocean has sold over 2 million albums worldwide.

Early life and education
Ocean was born Christopher Edwin Breaux on October 28, 1987, in Long Beach, California, to Calvin Cooksey, a singer and keyboardist, and Katonya Breaux Riley, an entrepreneur. His parents divorced when he was six years old, and he was raised by his mother. At age five, his family moved to New Orleans, Louisiana. Ocean was raised Christian and spent a brief period as a practicing Catholic.
Ocean's maternal grandfather Lionel McGruder Jr. was a father figure for Ocean after his father left the family. Lionel was a recovering drug addict and later served as a mentor at Alcoholics Anonymous and Narcotics Anonymous meetings. He would take Ocean to these meetings, which was the inspiration behind Ocean's song "Crack Rock" from Channel Orange. He also gave him the nickname Lonny, which Frank Ocean still uses today. He died in 2010 and Frank Ocean dedicated a song to him called "There Will Be Tears" on his mixtape Nostalgia, Ultra. He also mentioned him on his 2017 single "Lens".
After graduating from John Ehret High School in Marrero, Louisiana in 2005, Ocean enrolled in the University of New Orleans to study English. However, Hurricane Katrina struck New Orleans in August 2005, destroying his home and personal recording facility and forcing him to transfer to the University of Louisiana at Lafayette. He stayed there for a brief time before dropping out to focus on his music career.

grok_lead: Frank Ocean (born Christopher Edwin Breaux; October 28, 1987) is an American singer, songwriter, and rapper whose work blends elements of R&B, soul, and hip-hop. Born in Long Beach, California, Ocean relocated to New Orleans as a child and later moved to Los Angeles after Hurricane Katrina disrupted his college studies at the University of New Orleans. In 2010, he joined the hip-hop collective Odd Future, contributing vocals to projects like Tyler, the Creator's album Goblin, which helped build his early exposure in underground rap circles. His breakthrough came with the independent mixtape Nostalgia, Ultra (2011), featuring unauthorized samples that drew legal attention but showcased his songwriting prowess, including tracks later covered by artists like Kanye West. Ocean's debut studio album, Channel Orange (2012), released under Def Jam Recordings, debuted at number two on the Billboard 200 and earned critical praise for its narrative-driven songs addressing unrequited love and materialism. The album secured two Grammy Awards: Best Urban Contemporary Album and Best Rap/Sung Collaboration for "No Church in the Wild" with Jay-Z and Kanye West. In a Tumblr post coinciding with the album's release, Ocean disclosed a past same-sex relationship, a disclosure that preceded the project's commercial success and highlighted his personal candor amid industry speculation. His second album, Blonde (2016), self-released through his Boys Don't Cry imprint, topped the Billboard 200 and featured experimental production with minimal promotion, reflecting Ocean's shift toward artistic independence. Despite infrequent releases and tour cancellations, such as his 2023 Coachella withdrawal due to leg injuries, Ocean maintains influence through visual projects and occasional singles like "Chanel" (2017). His discography has sold millions, with Channel Orange certified platinum by the RIAA, underscoring a career defined by selective output and genre-blending innovation rather than prolific touring or media engagement.
